name: Eduardo Belmont Anderson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2013-2021); Hurun Global (2014-2023); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Eduardo Belmont is the owner and president of Belcorp, a door-to-door cosmetics company that operates in 14 Latin American countries and the U.S.
Hundreds of thousands of "beauty consultants" sell Belcorp products from their homes and in their neighborhoods.
Belcorp's revenues slipped to about $1.09 billion in 2016, a drop of some $100 million from the previous year.
forbes_facts: Eduardo and his brother Fernando used to run a jointly-owned cosmetics firm called Yanbal, but in 1988 they parted ways. Each now runs his own beauty enterprise.

name: Donald MacMillan
forbes_bio: Donald MacMillan is one of 21 billionaire heirs to Cargill, America's largest private company.
His great-grandfather, W.W. Cargill, founded the business as a single grain warehouse on the end of an Iowa railroad line in 1865.
He's one of nine billionaire siblings who inherited stakes in the company from their father John H.  MacMillan III, who died in 2008.
The family still owns roughly 90% of Cargill, which did $154 billion in 2025 sales across food, agriculture, financial and industrial divisions.

name: Akshay Arora
forbes_bio: Akshay Arora is the chairman of Mumbai-based pharma company Blue Jet Healthcare.
The 57-year-old company makes chemical agents that are used to enhance the visibility of body tissues in medical imaging, such as X rays, CT scans and MRI scans.
It also manufactures artificial sweeteners and pharma ingredients.
The company was listed on the Indian bourses in 2023 at a 10% premium to the issue price.
His son, Shiven, who studied business at Australia's Bond University, is the company's managing director.
forbes_facts: The company was established as Jet Chemicals in 1968 by his later father B.L.Arora.

name: Enrico Preziosi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2022)
forbes_bio: Enrico Preziosi is the founder and owner of Giochi Preziosi, Italy's largest toymaker.
He founded Giochi Preziosi in 1978 and the company licenses toys for brands including Disney, Fortnite and Pokemon.
In January 2020, he sold a 4% stake in the company to a group of investors including a Vatican-linked investment fund.
Preziosi was the president and owner of Italian soccer team Genoa CFC until he sold it to Miami-based investment firm 777 Partners in September 2021.

name: Ruth Porat
sec_insider_companies: Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) - President and CIO; Blackstone Inc. (BX) - Director
forbes_bio: Ruth Porat is president and chief investment officer of Google's parent company, Alphabet. She served as Chief Financial Officer at the company from 2015 to mid-2024.
Prior to Google, Porat rose through the ranks at Morgan Stanley over a 27-year career to become chief financial officer in 2010.
Porat has been praised for reining in spending on some of Google's "other bets," including delivering its own wireless service.
In 2020, Porat joined the board of Wall Street investment firm Blackstone.
Porat has spoken and written about being a breast cancer survivor; more than 15 years ago, she was diagnosed two times with the disease.
forbes_facts: As a proponent of "doing better on sexual harassment," she asked, "If you can get cars to self-drive, why can't we solve this?"

name: Kazutoshi Kobayashi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2018-2021)
forbes_bio: Kazutoshi Kobayashi is the president and CEO of  listed Japanese cosmetics manufacturer and retailer Kose.
He inherited a minority stake in Kose along with his brothers Takao and Masanori Kobayashi, who help him run the company.
Their grandfather, Kozaburo, started the company in 1946.
Kose exports its products to Hong Kong, China, Singapore and Malaysia.
